stem: The student wants to emphasize the historical significance of Vartenau's attachment relative to later developments in loom automation. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In the late 1700s, weavers in the town of Kessmer produced patterned linen for export.
• Weaver Ilse Vartenau designed a loom attachment that used notched wooden slats to raise warp threads in a set sequence.
• With the attachment, one weaver could produce a repeating damask pattern without the second worker earlier patterned looms required.
• Vartenau's attachment was patented in 1784.
• Joseph-Marie Jacquard's better-known punched-card loom, which also automated the lifting of warp threads, was introduced in 1804.
choices: Vartenau's attachment, which used notched wooden slats to raise warp threads in a set sequence, was patented in 1784.
Patented in 1784, Vartenau's attachment automated the lifting of warp threads two decades before Jacquard introduced his punched-card loom.
With Vartenau's attachment, a single weaver could produce a repeating damask pattern that had previously required a second worker.
Vartenau's attachment was the first device ever to automate pattern weaving, and Jacquard later copied its slat design.
explanation: The goal asks for significance relative to later developments, so you need the comparison that makes the 1784 date matter. Choice B sets Vartenau's attachment against Jacquard's 1804 loom and states the relationship outright: it did the same job two decades earlier.

A.why: You picked an accurate description of how the attachment worked and when it was patented. On its own, though, the bare date of 1784 says nothing about why it matters. Without Jacquard's 1804 loom beside it, nothing shows the attachment came earlier.

C.why: This choice does give a real benefit of the attachment, which is why it is tempting. But it compares the attachment with earlier looms, not later developments, so it misses the goal's specific comparison.

D.why: The notes never say the attachment was the first device of its kind or that Jacquard copied it. You went with a choice that claims more significance than the notes support.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Reyl's finding. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Many economists have assumed that raising the minimum wage leads employers to cut teenage workers' hours.
• Economist Tomasz Reyl studied 140 grocery stores along a county line; in 2019, one of the two counties raised its wage floor by 12%.
• He compared scheduled hours at stores in the two counties over the next 24 months.
• Teen workers' hours in the higher-wage county fell by less than 1%.
• Reyl drew hours from stores' scheduling software rather than from worker surveys.
choices: Reyl found that over 24 months, teen workers' hours at grocery stores in the higher-wage county fell by less than 1%.
Reyl's study, which drew on stores' scheduling software rather than worker surveys, compared hours in two neighboring counties.
Reyl's study proved that raising the minimum wage never reduces teen workers' hours, overturning a long-held assumption.
Contrary to the common assumption that a higher minimum wage cuts teen workers' hours, Reyl found their hours fell by less than 1%.
explanation: A finding is significant here because it challenges a background belief. Choice D places the result (hours fell by less than 1%) against the assumption that higher wages cut teen hours. It marks that relationship with "Contrary to."

A.why: This choice states the finding accurately but leaves out the assumption it contradicts. Without that background, a drop of less than 1% is just a number, and the reader can't see why it matters.

B.why: You focused on the study's method. The goal asks about the significance of the finding, and this choice never says what Reyl found.

C.why: One study of grocery stores in two counties can't show that minimum-wage increases "never" reduce hours. Hours did fall slightly, too. This choice turns a limited result into a universal claim.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of the kiln's age. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Kerevan Höyük is an archaeological site in central Anatolia.
• There, a team led by archaeologist Deniz Altay uncovered a kiln coated with fused glass residue.
• Radiocarbon dating of charcoal from the kiln indicates it was in use around 1850 BCE.
• Nearly all previously known glassmaking workshops in the region date to after 1500 BCE.
• The residue's chemical makeup matches that of glass beads found at a site 300 kilometers away.
choices: Dated to around 1850 BCE, the Kerevan Höyük kiln predates nearly all known glassmaking workshops in the region by more than three centuries.
Radiocarbon dating of charcoal from the kiln that Altay's team uncovered at Kerevan Höyük indicates that it was in use around 1850 BCE.
The glass residue in the Kerevan Höyük kiln chemically matches glass beads found at a site some 300 kilometers away.
Dated to around 1850 BCE, the Kerevan Höyük kiln is the oldest glassmaking site in the world, showing that glass was first made there.
explanation: The goal names its content: the kiln's age. The age matters only because the kiln is older than other workshops in the region. Choice A gives the date and the comparison to workshops dated after 1500 BCE, which is what makes the date significant.

B.why: This choice gives the date and how it was obtained, but 1850 BCE on its own carries no significance. You needed the comparison with the region's later workshops to show why the age matters.

C.why: The chemical match points to a different kind of significance, possibly trade, but it says nothing about the kiln's age. That is the specific thing the goal names.

D.why: The notes compare the kiln only with workshops in the region. They never say it is the oldest in the world or that glass was invented there.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the achievement of the bridge's engineers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Halvard Strait Bridge links two islands in a region prone to earthquakes.
• Its engineering team, led by Mirela Kostanjević, set the deck on 96 sliding pendulum bearings.
• The bearings let the deck shift up to 1.2 meters during shaking and then return to center.
• In 2023, a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck 30 kilometers from the bridge.
• The bridge reopened to traffic within six hours; two older bridges nearby stayed closed for months.
choices: Led by Mirela Kostanjević, the engineers set the Halvard Strait Bridge's deck on 96 sliding pendulum bearings.
In 2023, a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck 30 kilometers away, and two older bridges nearby stayed closed for months.
After a magnitude 7.1 earthquake in 2023, the engineers' bridge reopened within six hours, while two older nearby bridges stayed closed for months.
Because of its pendulum bearings, the Halvard Strait Bridge is the only bridge in the world that can survive a major earthquake undamaged.
explanation: An achievement is a successful outcome, and the notes make this one stand out by contrast. Choice C reports that the bridge reopened within six hours of a strong earthquake. It then uses "while" to set that against older bridges that stayed closed for months.

A.why: This choice tells you who led the work and what they built but never says what the design accomplished. You picked a description, not an achievement.

B.why: This choice gives the earthquake and the older bridges' failure, but it leaves out how the Halvard Strait Bridge performed. Without that outcome, the engineers' achievement disappears.

D.why: The notes compare the bridge only with two nearby bridges. Nothing supports calling it the only bridge in the world that could survive a major earthquake.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Tilde-4's performance in field trials. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sorghum is a cereal grain grown widely in dry regions.
• In 2021, plant breeder Amara Okonjo released a new sorghum variety called Tilde-4.
• Most sorghum varieties lose over 40% of their yield when seasonal rainfall drops below 350 millimeters.
• In field trials during a season with 290 millimeters of rain, Tilde-4 lost only 9% of its yield.
• Tilde-4's grains are reddish brown and slightly smaller than those of common varieties.
choices: Released by plant breeder Amara Okonjo in 2021, Tilde-4 is a sorghum variety with reddish-brown, slightly smaller grains.
In a season with just 290 millimeters of rain, Tilde-4 lost only 9% of its yield, whereas most sorghum varieties lose over 40% in such conditions.
In field trials during a season with 290 millimeters of rain, the sorghum variety Tilde-4 lost 9% of its yield.
In field trials, Tilde-4 proved fully resistant to drought, meaning it will end crop losses for sorghum growers in dry regions.
explanation: A 9% loss is significant only next to what usually happens. Choice B sets Tilde-4's loss against the more than 40% that most varieties lose below 350 millimeters of rain. It joins the two with "whereas," so the reader sees why the result matters.

A.why: This choice tells you who released Tilde-4 and what its grains look like, but nothing about how it performed in the trials. That performance is what the goal asks you to emphasize.

C.why: This is the closest near-miss. It reports the trial result accurately but leaves out the 40%-plus losses of other varieties. Without that comparison, a 9% loss could look ordinary or even bad.

D.why: Tilde-4 still lost 9% of its yield, so "fully resistant" contradicts the notes. A single trial season can't support the claim that it will end crop losses.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of the Torrivia lacustris fossil. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2021, a team led by paleobotanist Ilse Marten described Torrivia lacustris, a fossil plant from lake sediments in the Halvard Basin.
• The fossil preserves a seed enclosed in a fruit wall, a defining feature of flowering plants.
• Torrivia lacustris has been dated to about 131 million years ago.
• Before this find, the oldest known flowering-plant fossil with an enclosed seed was about 125 million years old.
choices: Described by Ilse Marten's team, Torrivia lacustris is a fossil plant from the Halvard Basin that has been dated to about 131 million years ago.
At about 131 million years old, Torrivia lacustris is roughly six million years older than any previously known flowering-plant fossil with an enclosed seed.
Torrivia lacustris, found in lake sediments in the Halvard Basin, preserves a seed enclosed in a fruit wall, a defining feature of flowering plants.
Torrivia lacustris shows that flowering plants first evolved in the Halvard Basin, about six million years earlier than researchers had assumed.
explanation: The fossil matters because it is older than every earlier example of its kind. Choice B gives its age and sets it beside the previous record of 125 million years, and that comparison is what makes the date significant.

A.why: You picked a choice with a date, but 131 million years means nothing on its own. Without the earlier 125-million-year record, the reader can't tell that this fossil is the oldest of its kind.

C.why: This choice describes what the fossil looks like and where it was found. It never says why the fossil matters.

D.why: The notes say only that this is the oldest known fossil of its kind. They don't say flowering plants first evolved in the Halvard Basin, and they don't say what researchers had assumed.

stem: The student wants to emphasize that the project succeeded in the area where critics expected it to fail. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2009, the city of Marrow Falls began replacing a three-kilometer elevated freeway with a ground-level boulevard.
• The project, led by planner Tomasz Reyna, added bus lanes and a linear park along the corridor.
• Critics predicted that drivers would avoid the boulevard and crowd onto nearby residential streets.
• Five years after the boulevard opened, traffic on those residential streets was 4 percent lower than before the project.
• Transit ridership along the corridor rose 38 percent over the same period.
choices: In 2009, planner Tomasz Reyna led Marrow Falls in replacing a three-kilometer elevated freeway with a boulevard, bus lanes, and a park.
Five years after Marrow Falls replaced its elevated freeway with a boulevard, transit ridership along the corridor had risen by 38 percent.
Critics warned that traffic would crowd onto nearby residential streets, yet five years after the boulevard opened, those streets carried 4 percent less traffic.
Critics warned that traffic would crowd onto nearby residential streets, and five years after the boulevard opened, those streets carried somewhat more traffic.
explanation: The goal names a specific success: the area critics doubted. The critics' concern was traffic on residential streets. Choice C states that concern and then gives the result that answers it, 4 percent less traffic.

A.why: This choice tells you who led the project and what was built. It says nothing about any outcome, so it can't show success.

B.why: Higher ridership is an achievement, but critics never predicted that ridership would fail. You stopped at 'success' and didn't check the second half of the goal.

D.why: The notes say residential traffic fell by 4 percent. This choice says it rose, which reverses the finding.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of the study's findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Injected vaccines produce antibodies in the blood but few in the lining of the nose, where many respiratory viruses first enter the body.
• Immunologist Priya Okonjo's team gave mice the same influenza vaccine either by injection or as a nasal spray.
• Only the nasal-spray group developed high antibody levels in the nasal lining.
• When exposed to the virus, injected mice avoided severe illness but often became infected.
• Most nasal-spray mice did not become infected at all.
choices: Okonjo's team gave mice the same influenza vaccine either by injection or as a nasal spray and then exposed both groups of mice to the virus.
Mice that received Okonjo's nasal-spray vaccine developed high levels of antibodies in the lining of the nose, where many respiratory viruses enter.
Okonjo's study shows that nasal-spray vaccines will protect people from influenza more effectively than injected vaccines currently do.
Unlike the injected version, Okonjo's nasal-spray vaccine produced antibodies where respiratory viruses enter, and it prevented most infections in mice.
explanation: The findings matter because the spray did something the injection could not: it put antibodies at the point of entry and stopped most infections. Choice D makes that comparison with 'Unlike the injected version' and states the outcome.

A.why: This choice describes the study's method. It reports no finding at all, so it can't show why the findings matter.

B.why: This is a real result, but the choice leaves out the comparison with injected vaccines and the drop in infections. Those are the parts that make the result significant.

C.why: The study used mice. Nothing in the notes supports a claim about protecting people or about how well current vaccines perform in humans.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the historical significance of the association's vacation policy. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Port Ellery Canners' Association was a cooperative founded by fish-cannery workers in 1921.
• Its members set their own wages and working hours by majority vote.
• In 1924, the association began giving each member one week of paid vacation per year.
• At the time, paid vacation was offered almost exclusively to salaried office staff, not to hourly industrial workers.
• Paid vacation for hourly workers did not become widespread until the 1940s.
choices: In 1924, two decades before paid vacation became widespread for hourly workers, the Port Ellery Canners' Association gave its members a paid week off.
Beginning in 1924, the Port Ellery Canners' Association, a workers' cooperative, gave each of its members one week of paid vacation every year.
Founded by fish-cannery workers in 1921, the Port Ellery Canners' Association let its members set their own wages and working hours by majority vote.
In 1924, the Port Ellery Canners' Association, like most industrial employers of the time, began giving each member one week of paid vacation.
explanation: The policy is historically significant because it came early, two decades before paid vacation became widespread for hourly workers. Choice A puts the 1924 date next to that later norm, so the reader can see the association was ahead of its time.

B.why: This choice gives the policy and the year but no point of comparison. A reader can't tell that 1924 was early unless the choice says when the practice became common.

C.why: This choice is about how the cooperative was founded and run. The goal is about the vacation policy, and this choice never mentions it.

D.why: The notes say paid vacation was almost never offered to hourly industrial workers then. Calling the association 'like most industrial employers' reverses that point.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Corvalite for jet-engine design. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ceramics withstand extreme heat but tend to shatter on impact.
• Earlier impact-resistant ceramics gained toughness from added metal, which softens above 900°C.
• Some jet-engine parts reach temperatures of 1,300°C.
• Materials scientist Kenji Avelar's team developed Corvalite, a metal-free ceramic built in thin layers modeled on mother-of-pearl.
• In tests at 1,300°C, Corvalite cracked under impact but did not shatter.
choices: Corvalite, a metal-free ceramic developed by Kenji Avelar's team, is built in thin layers modeled on the structure of mother-of-pearl.
Because it does not shatter, Corvalite has replaced the metal-containing ceramics that were previously used in the parts of jet engines.
Unlike earlier tough ceramics, whose added metal softens above 900°C, Corvalite resisted shattering at the 1,300°C some jet-engine parts reach.
In tests conducted at 1,300°C, Corvalite, a ceramic developed by Avelar's team, cracked under impact but did not shatter.
explanation: Corvalite matters for jet engines because it stays tough at a temperature where earlier tough ceramics fail. Choice C includes all three parts of that argument: the 900°C limit of the older materials, Corvalite's performance at 1,300°C, and the link to jet-engine temperatures.

A.why: This choice describes Corvalite's structure and who made it. It never says what the material can do or why that matters for jet engines.

B.why: The notes describe test results only. Nothing says Corvalite has been put into jet engines or has replaced anything.

D.why: This is the test result, but on its own 1,300°C is just a number. Without the 900°C limit of earlier ceramics and the link to jet engines, the reader can't see why it matters.
